verdict.summary: A demo-environment integration key works within the hour, but every production key has to be owned by a paid (or partner) production account, and DocuSign's docs say a public integration that many customers authorize needs Partner Program membership. In 2026 forum threads, small ISVs were turned away (a 20-employee minimum and a rejected Business Pro account), and DocuSign support pointed them to having customers bring their own integration key.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Free developer account, create an integration in the Developer Console (Demo toggle), add a redirect URI and secret, then run the auth-code flow against account-d.docusign.com.

timeToProd.assumes: A public integration that any DocuSign customer can authorize with their own account, which needs Partner Program acceptance plus Go-Live. A private custom integration on your own paid account can be promoted automatically the same day, or after a 24–48 hour manual review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Partner Program application decision, then the Go-Live check (automatic, or manual review typically 24–48 hours), plus a one-time identity verification on the production account

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The 24–48 hour manual review figure is from DocuSign's docs. The Partner Program timeline isn't published, and forum threads show applications rejected outright, so the range is our estimate for an accepted applicant.

verdict.cost: A paid DocuSign production account (forum reports say Business Pro may be rejected and a custom enterprise plan required) or Partner Program membership. Envelope billing depends on the integration classification.

prerequisites.why: Integration keys are created and tested in the demo environment first.

prerequisites.item: A paid or partner production DocuSign account with admin access

prerequisites.why: The docs say you need to join the Partner Program to launch a public integration; embedded use needs an ISV Embed licence.
REST integrations must use OAuth 2.0 to pass Go-Live, unless you get a policy exception.

scopeTiers.impact: Send, read and track envelopes for the consenting user. 'extended' gives a fresh ~30-day refresh token on each refresh so users can stay connected. Review here means Go-Live, not per-scope review.

Reading agreement data across the repository, which is what an AI contract agent often wants. The account also needs access to that API.

steps.title: Create a developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a free DocuSign developer account (demo environment).

steps.title: Create an integration in the Developer Console
steps.detail: Click + Add, keep the toggle on Demo, copy the demo client ID and secret, and add redirect URIs.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The Developer Console is in open beta; the legacy Apps and Keys page still works.

steps.title: Implement OAuth and base-URI discovery
steps.detail: Auth-code (or PKCE) against account-d.docusign.com/oauth/auth, exchange at /oauth/token, call /oauth/userinfo once to get the account's base_uri and cache it.

steps.title: Use Connect webhooks instead of polling
steps.detail: Subscribe to Connect for envelope status. Polling one envelope more than once per 15 minutes is flagged and can fail Go-Live.

steps.title: Decide the integration classification
steps.detail: Choose Private custom, Third-party integration key (customer BYOK), Public (Partner Program) or Embedded (ISV Embed licence). This drives Go-Live and envelope billing.

steps.title: Apply to the Partner Program (public integrations)
steps.detail: Apply through the partner portal. Forum reports say applicants under 20 employees were rejected.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 20-employee rule is from a community post (unverified).

steps.title: Get a production account and verify identity
steps.detail: Have admin on a paid or partner production account; complete the one-time identity verification if 'Verification required' appears.

steps.title: Submit for Go-Live
steps.detail: In the Developer Console choose the integration type, Save, then Submit for Go-Live approval.

steps.title: Automatic promotion or manual review
steps.detail: Eligible apps go live automatically; otherwise status is Pending approval or Declined, with manual reviews typically 24–48 hours.

steps.title: Configure production settings
steps.detail: Toggle to Production, copy the production client ID/secret, and re-add redirect URIs and secrets; they aren't copied from demo.

blockers.symptom: "Your account doesn't support promoting an integration key to production" in the Go-Live dialog
blockers.cause: The chosen production account's plan (Business Pro was reported) doesn't support key promotion.
blockers.fix: Use a plan that supports it (sales quoted a custom enterprise plan in one thread), join the Partner Program, or have customers use their own key.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: From a July 2026 community thread; DocuSign hadn't clarified the policy there.

blockers.symptom: Partner Program application rejected for a small company
blockers.cause: Applicants reportedly need at least 20 employees.
blockers.fix: DocuSign support suggested having customers create an integration key in their own account (Third-party integration key) for now.

blockers.cause: The app needs manual review or more information, or the production account needs a one-time identity verification ('Verification required').
blockers.fix: Download the review logs, fix errors, finish identity verification, and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Go-Live fails although calls look fine
blockers.cause: The review checks your 20 most recent API calls (login and userinfo calls excluded) for errors and polling violations; requesting the same envelope within 15 minutes counts as polling, and legacy or OAuth 1.0 auth isn't accepted.
blockers.fix: Poll at 20-minute intervals or use Connect, cache document lists, and make 20 clean OAuth 2.0 calls right before submitting.

blockers.symptom: Production calls fail with invalid redirect URI or invalid_client after going live
blockers.cause: Secrets and redirect URIs aren't copied from demo to production.
blockers.fix: Add them again in the production version of the integration.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error strings are inferred.

blockers.cause: Per-envelope GET limits, or userinfo limits of 25,000/hour per user and 50,000/hour per integration key.
blockers.fix: Cache base_uri once per user and switch to Connect.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 8 hours (expires_in 28800). Refresh tokens last about 30 days; with the extended scope each refresh issues a new full-lifetime token, so users can stay connected indefinitely.
Accounts get 3,000 API calls per hour by default, shared across all apps, plus a 30-second burst limit of 500 in production (200 in demo).
Production base URIs differ by data centre ({server}.docusign.net); get them from /oauth/userinfo rather than hard-coding.
The integration key is copied, not moved, to production, so the same client ID keeps working in demo.
DocuSign also runs an official MCP server with setup guides for Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot and others, which may suit agents better than raw REST.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Seen in the docs navigation (/platform/mcp-server/); we didn't review its access terms.

nuances.text: The integration classification you pick changes how envelopes are billed on your production account.
